title: Genset Maintenance Technician
description:
Summary
The Genset Maintenance Technician is responsible for the preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, and servicing of diesel and gas-powered generators across company facilities. This role ensures reliable backup power supply, compliance with safety standards, and optimal performance of all generator sets (gensets).
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Generator Maintenance & Servicing
Perform
scheduled preventive maintenance
(oil changes, filter replacements, coolant checks, battery testing).
Conduct
load bank testing
to verify generator performance under load.
Inspect and maintain
fuel systems, cooling systems, exhaust systems, and electrical components
.
2. Troubleshooting & Repairs
Diagnose and repair
mechanical failures
(engine issues, fuel injectors, turbochargers, belts, pumps).
Troubleshoot
electrical faults
(AVR, control panels, wiring, circuit breakers, voltage regulators).
Replace defective parts and ensure proper reassembly and testing.
3. Emergency Response
Provide
24/7 on-call support
for generator failures and power outages.
Rapidly diagnose issues and implement corrective actions to minimize downtime.
4. Documentation & Compliance
Maintain detailed
service logs, work orders, and maintenance records
(CMMS or manual logs).
Ensure compliance with
OSHA, NFPA 110, EPA emissions, and company safety policies
.
Track
fuel consumption, runtime hours, and spare parts inventory
.
5. Installation & Commissioning Support
Assist in
new generator installations, ATS setups, and synchronization checks
.
Verify proper operation before handover to operations.
Job Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
(required).
Technical certification
in Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, Generator Maintenance, or related field (preferred).
Manufacturer certifications
(Cummins, Kohler, Caterpillar, Generac) are a plus.
3+ years
of hands-on experience in
generator maintenance and repair
.
Familiarity with
diesel/gas generators (10kVA – 2000kVA+)
.
Knowledge of
ATS, load banks, and paralleling systems
.
Mechanical:
Engine diagnostics (compression tests, fuel system troubleshooting). Ability to disassemble, repair, and reassemble generator components.
Electrical:
Proficiency with
multimeters, meggers, and diagnostic tools
. Understanding of
control panels, wiring diagrams, and synchronization
.
Soft Skills:
Strong problem-solving and attention to detail. Ability to work independently and under pressure. Good communication for reporting and team coordination.
Field Work:
On-site servicing at multiple locations.
Physical Demands:
Lifting (25 kg), working in confined spaces, outdoor repairs.
Shift Work:
Rotational on-call duty for emergencies.
Travel to all sites for repair and maintenance works.
